title: Neuron-Anchored Rule Extraction for Large Language Models via Contrastive Hierarchical Ablation

problem.claim: Explainable AI seeks to express LLM decision logic symbolically and ground it in internal mechanisms.

gap.claim: Existing methods either learn ungrounded symbolic surrogates or require costly, hypothesis-driven neuron interventions.

contributions.claim: MechaRule grounds rule extraction in LLM circuits by localizing sparse agonist activations whose ablation disrupts rule-related behavior.

Under a fixed baseline/flip regime with k much less than N, overtopping supports adaptive group testing with confidence-guided conservative pruning using O(k?ogNoverk +k) interventions over N candidates.
Agonists are localized more reliably using data splits aligned with close-to-faithful rule behavior, with spectral splits as a rule-free fallback.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On arithmetic and jailbreaking, MechaRule recalls 97.0% of highest-effect agonists at 2.14% of exhaustive-ablation cost on average.
Ablating localized agonists eliminates 97.6-100.0% of eligible correct arithmetic answers and jailbreaks.
Ablation can correct arithmetic errors by up to 72.8% or induce jailbreaks by up to 32.5%.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets symbolic explanations grounded in LLM mechanisms and addresses limitations of existing rule-extraction and mechanistic-interpretability methods.
MechaRule localizes sparse agonist activations and uses their behavioral effect under ablation to ground extracted rules in circuits.
The pipeline relies on overtopping, adaptive group testing, and data splits selected for faithful rule behavior or used as a spectral fallback.
Experiments on arithmetic and jailbreaking report high agonist recall at low ablation cost and substantial behavioral changes after ablation.

source_observation.claim: A few high-effect activations can remain detectable within larger groups and dominate weaker activations in a fixed baseline/flip regime.

interpretation.claim: Hierarchical search may reduce intervention cost when influential components exhibit concentration and overtopping.

application.claim: Use adaptive group testing with conservative confidence-guided pruning to search large candidate sets.

exception.claim: The stated complexity applies to the fixed baseline/flip regime when k is much smaller than N.

source_observation.claim: Localization is more reliable on splits aligned with close-to-faithful rule behavior, while unfaithful splits degrade localization.

interpretation.claim: The quality of the data split can materially affect mechanistic localization results.

application.claim: Prefer behavior-aligned splits and use spectral splits when a rule-based split is unavailable.

exception.claim: Spectral splits are described as a rule-free fallback rather than a universally faithful split.

unknowns: Dataset sizes, model configurations, and task construction are not specified.
Definitions of agonist, eligible answers, confidence guarantees, and rule faithfulness are not detailed.
The abstract does not describe the exact extracted rule format or intervention protocol.
